cases.evidence: Emitted the object NP as a standalone piece; the translation omitted 'discovered' and read the disease as predicated of the name (contradiction 0.962).
cases.proposed_rule: Demote any candidate boundary that would end on a bare noun phrase (object) when an earlier chunk contains a personal name and the clause's finite verb linking them is not included in the same chunk.

cases.evidence: Boundary after the ethnonym led to wrong attachment of the following locative/appositive ('in Canada' / ', a Greenlander, in Greenland'), producing a premature reading (contradiction 0.8994).
cases.proposed_rule: Lower rank for boundaries that end on an ethnonym/demonym when the same clause later contains a locative PP or comma-set appositive; wait to emit until the locative/appositive scope is visible.

example_pair.input: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

cases.evidence: The segmenter cut inside coordinated predicates with a shared postmodifier ('for the club'), causing the translator to attach the PP incorrectly and lowering adequacy.
cases.proposed_rule: Demote boundaries that split coordinated verb phrases joined by 'and' or 'or' when a following PP or comparative (e.g., 'for the club', 'than X') appears to modify both predicates; prefer placing the boundary after the shared postmodifier.

example_pair.input: No one else has ever made more appearances or scored more goals for the club than Bobek.
example_pair.output: No one else has ever made more appearances or scored more goals for the club than Bobek. <SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Cut inside a participial modifier; the emitted piece misassigned the experiencer/agent and produced an incorrect first-piece translation (low adequacy).
cases.proposed_rule: Rank low any boundary that would cut inside a non‑finite participial modifier (V‑ing/V‑ed clause) attached to a subject; keep the participial phrase with its head noun or wait for the main predicate.

example_pair.input: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.
example_pair.output: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements. <SEG:1>

summary: The prompt is over‑confident about boundaries that fall at commas and that separate nouns/ethnonyms/participial clauses from the predicates or shared modifiers that determine their scope. Coverage is fine, so prefer priority fixes: demote (do not ban) comma‑adjacent cuts when they separate a person name from a subsequent NP object, an ethnonym from a later locative/appositive, coordinated verbs from their shared PP/comparative, or when they split a participial modifier from its subject. Because rank_lift is positive, reordering these features should reduce high‑impact contradictions without shrinking candidate coverage.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`
